summary: SpaceX is scheduled to attempt a historic Starship test flight today featuring a first-ever double-catch landing attempt, while United Launch Alliance prepares for its first Vulcan Centaur launch in nine months. In defense space developments, SpaceX successfully launched a second classified mission for the U.S. Space Force within six days, the Pentagon approved a $150 million loan to Rocket Lab to boost launch cadence, and the Space Development Agency is exploring the integration of SpaceX laser communication terminals with missile tracking satellites. Internationally, Germany and Poland contracted defense firm SATIM to analyze military satellite imagery. In civil space oversight, a U.S. Senate committee initiated confirmation proceedings for nominees to serve as NASA’s chief financial officer and inspector general. On the scientific front, the European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope published its initial data release toward building a 3D cosmological map, while NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope identified target surveys for the upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Commercial activity saw European startup Gama raise €15 million in seed funding for solar array supply chains, while AST SpaceMobile outlined plans to develop its own launch vehicle. Looking ahead, a Pakistani astronaut is scheduled to become the first international visitor to China's Tiangong space station later this month.
